Elated

ih-LAY-tid -- three syllables, stress on the second syllable, LAY. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Elated is extremely happy and excited.

Priya was elated to find her lost ring glinting in the garden soil.

Worked Example

The roster goes up at 3:00. At 3:01, Jen finds her name on the varsity list -- and for the rest of the day she cannot stop grinning, texting, and replaying the moment in her head.

Jen is elated: lifted to a sudden emotional high by one specific piece of good news. Elated is situational and usually temporary -- it spikes when the news lands and fades as life returns to normal. That trigger is what separates it from a sanguine outlook, which needs no good news at all.

How Elated Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

overjoyed

overjoyed: filled with great happiness

thrilled

thrilled: very excited and pleased

jubilant

jubilant: celebrating success loudly and openly

Antonyms

crestfallen

crestfallen: sad and disappointed after a letdown

downcast

downcast: low in spirits

How Strong Is It? — thrilled → elated → jubilant

thrilled vs. elated

thrilled vs. elated: Thrilled is the everyday, slightly weaker word -- you can be thrilled by a roller coaster or a small gift -- while elated describes a real emotional high set off by news that matters.

jubilant vs. elated

jubilant vs. elated: Jubilant is the strongest and loudest: an elated student may only beam quietly at her desk, but a jubilant crowd sings, chants, and celebrates out loud.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — e-

prefix — e-: out, up (Latin ex-)

root — lat-

root — lat-: carried (Latin latus, past participle of ferre 'to carry')

suffix — -ed

suffix — -ed: having been made (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Elated comes from Latin elatus, 'carried out, lifted up' -- e- ('up, out') plus latus ('carried'). To be elated is to be carried up above your ordinary mood, lifted by a piece of good news the way a wave lifts a boat.

Use the root in a new word: translate

Use the root in a new word: translate: It took her all evening to translate the letter from Portuguese.

Root Check

Word Choice

Elated needs a trigger: elated BY the news, elated WHEN the letter came. It names the spike, not the temperament -- sanguine is the steady outlook, euphoria is the even higher (and shorter) peak, and elated sits between them: a genuine high, tied to one happy event.
